title: Propagate delegated actor context through the Quest adapter instead of declaring every write human
summary: Propagate delegated actor context through the Quest adapter instead of declaring every write human
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

Source-confirmed attribution gap: src/adapters/quest.ts defines ACTOR_FLAGS = ["--actor", "lore", "--actor-kind", "human"] and uses them for Quest writes, including adapter migration operations. A delegated caller cannot preserve its declared agent identity and accountable human through this constant.
Reproduce by inspecting/capturing the Quest subprocess argv for a Lore-triggered edit from a delegated-agent session: it declares actor lore, actor-kind human regardless of the caller. The source constant is the direct evidence; this finding does not claim that principal:null proves authorization failure or durable audit loss.
Expected: an explicit supported actor-context input is validated and propagated according to Quest's contract. Human and delegated-agent invocations should remain distinguishable. Related completed work LCLI-407 verifies edit semantics but does not resolve this caller attribution gap.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Lore accepts and validates explicit human or delegated-agent actor context for Quest writes.
Delegated writes pass the agent identity and accountable human instead of hardcoded human attribution.
Adapter tests assert argv for edits and migration paths and verify any promised persisted attribution; missing context fails before writes.

implementationNotes: Fixed. TrackerAdapter's quest.ts gains QuestActorContext (id, kind: human|delegated-agent, accountableHumanId), an explicit actor option plus LORE_QUEST_ACTOR/LORE_QUEST_ACTOR_KIND/LORE_QUEST_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN env-var fallback, resolved and validated only at the point of an actual write (create/edit/migration apply/rollback) -- read-only ops never need it. Missing context, an invalid kind, or a delegated-agent with no accountable human all fail before any spawn, mirroring Quest's own write-actor contract. Six new adapter tests cover argv for edit/create/migration apply+rollback under a delegated-agent actor, the three missing/invalid/no-spawn cases, and the env-var fallback path. Per campaign rule, not calling this Done until opum-cli-e2e's cross-product row passes against a real lore build -- filing that now.
Session pre-compact at 2026-09-07T18:31:49Z. Branch dev, 5 uncommitted file(s). Written by the opum-workflow pre-compact hook, not by the model.

Qualified in opum-cli-e2e (PR opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#56, branch task-25-pending-links-orphans): 3 new cross-product rows in suites/40-cross-product.mjs assert fail-closed with no/invalid actor context and success once a valid delegated-agent actor + accountable human are declared via LORE_QUEST_ACTOR/_ACTOR_KIND/_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN. Verified against a real lore binary built from origin/dev tip (d45623a) via git archive (never a working-tree checkout): all 3 rows pass against dev-tip, the 2 fail-closed rows correctly fail against currently-published 0.4.6 (proves the rows exercise the fix, not vacuous passes). Full cross-product suite 27/27 with dev-tip lore + quest 0.4.0. Note from opum-cli-e2e: Quest 0.4.0 has no on-disk actor/accountableHuman field and no audit/history command, so this only proves fail-closed-vs-succeeds behavior at the boundary, not which identity reached Quest -- narrower than full attribution corroboration, flagged so nobody assumes otherwise. Also: this fix is breaking for any existing caller of a Quest-writing lore command (link/unlink/Backlog migration) with no actor context declared -- opum-cli-e2e had to add harness-wide LORE_QUEST_ACTOR/_ACTOR_KIND/_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN env defaults to keep 3 previously-passing rows green. Follow-up: checking this repo's own docs/CI/examples for the same exposure before this ships.
